Lowlights

  • Mid-sprint scope added is 57% of planned (target ≤25%). Most mid-sprint adds landed on NDB-2.11 (28% of those tickets), then NDB-2.9 (21%). 15 teams are above that — highest: HADR 272%, YODA 137%, DBMOVE 105%, LOKI 83%, BOBA 83%. HADR · YODA · DBMOVE · LOKI · BOBA

  • 531 sprint items sit in Resolved (awaiting QA verification) right now. QA queue

Appendix — definitions, method, caveats
  • Who is in this report: only assignees in Team-BharatKumar-Beedu-Org or Team-Ashish-Kumar-Org (today's JIRA group membership). Work by people outside those groups is excluded.
  • Window: 26 sprint slots (S34–S59, 2025-04-09 → end of S59). The current open slot is excluded so numbers don't move under the reader.
  • Source: JIRA Sprint Report for every board 2888 sprint in the window (board → Reports → Sprint Report). Per-sprint Completed / Not Completed / Removed counts match that page. Click a heatmap cell → sprint name to compare.
  • Unit: one issue listed in one sprint's report. Items = Completed + Not Completed + Removed (+ completed outside the sprint).
  • Done (sprint math) = JIRA "Completed Issues" when the sprint closed. Planned = items − mid-sprint adds (*). Say/Do = planned completed ÷ planned. Completion = all completed ÷ all items. Scope added = added ÷ planned.
  • Dev-finished say/do (second heatmap) = same planned membership; Do = status at sprint close was Resolved or Closed. Compare to JIRA Completed say/do to see QA lag inside the same sprint window.
  • Tickets that slipped = distinct tickets that appeared in "Issues Not Completed" at least once in the selected range (not a sum of per-sprint rows). "Still open today" uses each ticket's current JIRA status.
  • Dev → QA lag: Dev finishes at Resolved; QA finishes at Closed. Waiting age = days since Resolved for tickets still in Resolved. Close lag = days Resolved→Closed from changelog (Closed Bug/Improvement sample). This is a QA bandwidth signal — not a sprint say/do failure by itself.
  • Status now vs at close: KPI tiles, chronic list and QA queue use live status / fix versions fetched at report generation. The sprint drill-down keeps the status from the Sprint Report (at close) so it matches JIRA.
  • Chronic carry-over: tickets planned into 3+ sprints in the window (non-removed appearances). Tabs split Still open / Resolved (awaiting QA) / Closed. Shipped in = earliest released fix version dated on/after the closed date.
  • Discipline timeline: splits say/do into phases where the level shifts ≥8 pts for ≥3 sprints. Release gates come from the curated releaseGateDates calendar (CC / CG / PG / GA; hollow ◇ = superseded date).
  • Mid-sprint churn by release: unique mid-sprint-added tickets attributed by current fix version (excludes master / long-lived buckets). Share is of those tickets that have a product fix version.
  • Trend = say/do of the last 3 sprints vs the 3 before. Teams with no sprint in the last 3 slots are hidden from rankings unless you show retired teams.
  • Velocity streams exclude portfolio types (Feature, Initiative, Epic, X-FEAT, Capability); headline tiles include every issue type, as the Sprint Report does. QA verification = Bug/Improvement completed and Closed, ×0.33 (adjusted count, not story points).
  • Org roll-up: manager = Team-*-DirectReports. With a scope filter, each person rolls up under the matching scope org (e.g. BharatKumar Beedu / Ashish Kumar). Groups reflect membership at generation time. If a group owner's JIRA account is inactive (they left), that group is skipped — people fall through to another live DirectReports group when they have one, otherwise Unmapped (manager left).
  • Links: one sprint → its JIRA Sprint Report. Narrow filters (team / manager / short range) → ticket search. When a search URL would be too long for JIRA (Tomcat header limit), the number stays plain and a copy JQL button appears — paste into Issues → Advanced search. Multi-sprint JIRA searches show distinct tickets and omit removed issues, so totals can differ from summed per-sprint counts.
  • Sprint slots use the 3-week cadence with S60 start = 2026-10-07; each scrum team's own sprint name may differ.
  • Latest slot still closing: 5 sprints were active at generation; their Sprint Report numbers may still move.
